- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, indicating an overshoot after spikes, followed by premature mean reversion.
- Model shows strong lag in adjusting to recent price drops — often underreacts to downward momentum in history.
- When true prices rise sharply (e.g., >10% from prior day), model fails to fully capture the magnitude, underestimating the spike.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after spikes, leading to premature price declines that don’t match actual volatility.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent high prices, leading to overconfidence in continued upward trends.
- Model underestimates volatility in late forecast periods, particularly when true prices show sustained upward momentum.
- Correction should involve smoothing out early forecast peaks and adjusting downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
